title: Add multi-region availability SLO template + error budget burn calculators
author: Aisha Bello
release_notes:
- New SLO template for multi-region availability (Hosted API + Dedicated).
- New burn-rate calculators that support region-level impairment classification and multi-window alerting.
- Example queries and config snippets for Redwood’s failover dashboards/alerts.
description:
Summary: This PR adds a first-class template for measuring multi-region availability and associated error budget burn, intended for Redwood’s Regional Failover Automation Upgrade. It includes: (1) a reusable SLO definition for multi-region availability, (2) calculators/helpers for computing burn rates over multiple windows (e.g., 5m/1h, 30m/6h), and (3) documentation + examples showing how to classify region-level events vs partial degradation.

Motivation: We currently have per-region availability SLOs and ad-hoc dashboards, but no consistent way to answer: “Are we meeting the multi-region availability SLO as experienced by customers?” During regional impairment, traffic shifts can make per-region SLOs look worse while customer-visible availability remains acceptable (or the reverse if routing is unhealthy). This template standardizes measurement so we can (a) drive alerting off the right numerator/denominator, (b) compare failover controller changes against a stable baseline, and (c) report error budget burn consistently.

Design notes: The template is intentionally opinionated about inputs and aggregation: (a) uses a customer-visible request success metric (2xx/3xx) as the primary signal, with explicit handling for controlled load shedding (e.g., 429/503 with Retry-After) via an allowlist; (b) aggregates across “serving regions” for a route/tier, so the SLO reflects the experience of the routing system rather than any single region; (c) supports tagging/annotation of “region-level event” windows to avoid mixing planned failover tests with organic incidents in retros.

What’s included: - Template: `multi_region_availability` SLO definition with parameters for `service` (hosted-api, dedicated-gateway), `route`, `tenant_tier`, and `region_group` (e.g., us/eu) so we can respect residency constraints in downstream configs. - Calculators: helpers to compute availability ratio, error budget remaining, and burn rates over multiple windows; includes a small library of guardrails (min request volume, missing-data policy) to reduce false positives. - Examples: sample configs and queries for dashboards/alerts used by SRE during failover game days.

What’s NOT included: - No automatic wiring into alert manager/paging routes in this PR (that stays in observability-pack). - No changes to production SLO targets or contract language; this is a toolkit building block.

Validation: - Added unit tests for burn-rate math and missing-data behavior. - Added golden tests for query generation for both Hosted API and Dedicated flavors. - Ran `slo-toolkit validate` against a staging metric snapshot and confirmed outputs match existing dashboard calculations within rounding error.

Follow-ups: - Observability-pack PR will consume the template and roll it into the failover dashboards + burn alerts bundle. - We should align the allowlist semantics for Retry-After responses with the API gateway overload changes (see ENG-2419) so availability measurement matches customer guidance.

conversation: Allison Grant (review): Can we be explicit about what HTTP codes count as “good” for availability? Specifically: where do we land on 429/503 w/ Retry-After during overload? I don’t want the SLO to incentivize returning 200s on unhealthy systems, but we also shouldn’t page for intentional shedding when we’re within failover guardrails.

Aisha Bello (author): Agree. I added `success_status_classes` + `allowed_shed_statuses` as separate knobs with documented defaults. Defaults: 2xx/3xx good; 429/503 are excluded from “good” but can be optionally excluded from “bad” if `shed_is_not_customer_visible=true` AND `retry_after_present=true`. Docs call out that this should match gateway guidance and be used sparingly.

Miles Thornton (review): The event classification section is good, but we need deterministic language: what makes something a “region-level event” vs partial? Also, can you ensure the template can represent a region-group (e.g., EU-only) so we don’t accidentally normalize away residency constraints?

Aisha Bello (author): Updated docs with explicit classification guidance: region-level event is when routing for a region_group fails to serve within policy (reachability + error burn corroboration), and multi-region SLO is evaluated within that region_group. Added `region_group` parameter and made it required in the template; examples show `region_group=eu` vs `region_group=global` for hosted routes that can spill globally.
Sergio Costa (review): Nit: renderers should cap label cardinality in generated queries. If `route` is unbounded we’ll regret it. Can we add a note or safeguard?

Aisha Bello (author): Added a `dimension_allowlist` option + docs recommending routing-level aggregation for alerts (route_group) and using high-cardinality route only for dashboards. Also added a validation warning when the template is configured with >4 dimensions for alerting use-cases.
Paula Mendes (review): Please add an example that matches what PM-513 wants: a monthly rollup view (error budget remaining) and the standard burn windows for paging.

Aisha Bello (author): Added examples for (a) monthly rollup via 30d window query, (b) burn windows 5m/1h and 30m/6h with recommended thresholds. Also updated README section “Multi-window burn alerts”.
CI Bot: Checks passed: lint, unit-tests, golden-tests, build, docs-link-check.
Allison Grant (approval): Approved. Thanks for tightening the shed semantics and validation warnings.
Miles Thornton (approval): Approved. Region-group requirement is the right call.
